text:
The scoreboard said NYR by two, but the chances said this was close to a coin flip. Vladislav Gavrikov opened the scoring late in the first period on a wrist shot that carried only a 2% chance of going in, and the Rangers took the lead into the second despite UTA matching them in chance quality, 0.7 expected goals to 0.72. UTA then outplayed them in the middle period, 1.59 to 1.16, and Nick Schmaltz tied it on the power play with a backhand at 14:29.

The third period decided it. NYR out-chanced UTA 2.26 to 1.28 by the period-by-period numbers, and the goals followed. Gabe Perreault put them ahead 2-1 early in the period, and J.T. Miller deflected one in at 12:47 to make it 3-1. Andrew Peeke pulled UTA within one at 14:57, but Eeli Tolvanen's wrist shot at 18:45, a 40% chance and the best look among the goals, sealed it. Tye Kartye had a 68% chance in the same period that Karel Vejmelka turned away, so the margin could have been wider.

By the full-game measure, NYR deserved the win 53% of the time, a slim edge. UTA produced 69 shot attempts to 55 and 3.57 expected goals to NYR's 4.13, and it went 1 for 2 on the power play while NYR went 0 for 4. Igor Shesterkin made the difference between the two teams, saving 1.57 goals more than expected on 30 shots, while Vejmelka saved 0.74 more than expected. Gavrikov finished with a goal and an assist and took the first star.
